If I’m alone in my apartment and the wind picks up, or the sky goes that strange greenish color before a storm, I just… lock up. I’ll stand there by the window or in the hallway and feel like my legs stop working. It’s like my body decides not to move, even when I’m telling myself it’s just weather.

It started maybe a few months ago, around the time my supervisor began pushing harder on my thesis deadline. I’ve always been a bit uneasy with storms and the dark, but lately if I’m walking home and the streetlights are patchy or I hear thunder in the distance, I can’t keep going. I’ll freeze on the sidewalk or in the stairwell of my building, heart racing, waiting for it to pass.

What worries me is that I can’t fully explain why it feels so threatening. Part of me knows it’s probably nothing, but in the moment it feels like there’s… something out there, or something bad about to happen, and I just can’t make myself move.
D012-D005_h001.question_a:
It’s embarrassing to talk about because it sounds childish, but it’s gotten out of hand. I’m terrified of thunderstorms and deep water. Not like “I don’t like them,” but full-on panic.

If there’s a storm in the forecast, I start checking the weather app obsessively. If I see dark clouds rolling in, my heart starts pounding and I feel like I can’t breathe. I know storms can actually be dangerous—lightning, flooding—so in my head it feels totally justified, but my reaction is way over the top. During that big storm about six months ago, I was alone in my apartment and I just froze on the couch for almost an hour, muscles locked, afraid to even walk to the bathroom because the windows are there.

With water, I avoid lakes, boats, even walking over bridges if I can. I’m scared of falling in, getting pulled under. I can picture it so vividly that I just stop moving—my legs literally won’t step closer. This has been going on for at least a couple of years, but it’s gotten worse over the last year with thesis stress. I don’t think anyone’s out to get me or anything like that—I’m scared of the storm itself, the water itself.
D012-D005_h001.question_b:
It’s been going on for a little over a year now. I know this is going to sound strange, but it isn’t just that I’m scared of storms or the dark in a normal way. When there’s thunder or heavy rain, I’m sure it’s targeted at me, like the weather is being controlled to punish me or expose my research.

When that fear hits, I just freeze—I literally can’t move, like if I stay perfectly still they can’t track me.

It’s not that I think the blood is cursed or that something bizarre will happen; I know, logically, it’s just blood. I go out of my way to avoid it. During fire drills or sports events, I make sure another administrator is “on call” for injuries. I picture the teeth, the weight, the fall.
